inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 336.1m shares on issue at 30-Jun-2026 (FY26 Appendix 4E NTA table, includes employee-trust shares) + 2.3m dilutive rights (FY26 note 5: diluted 335.9m less basic 333.6m weighted). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution too would double-count. No non-SBC issuance modelled (e2open was 100% debt-funded).
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 Annual Report note 22 cash-flow reconciliation: share-based payment expense USD 80.3m (FY25 48.7m). Includes ~USD 18m capitalised into intangibles (P&L portion 62.3m, note 19), so the full 80.3m is charged because cash capex excludes it. EquityAwardTaxes = 0: plans are settled in shares issued to the employee trust (proceeds from issue of shares 84.4 = treasury shares acquired 84.4), no net-share-settlement tax outflow.
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in USD (WiseTech switched presentation currency AUD->USD from H1 FY2025; FY2016-FY2024 history is AUD). Per-share values computed in USD and converted to AUD at 1/AUDUSD = 1/0.7026 = 1.4233 AUD per USD (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-09-25T06:36Z). Parity check: US OTC line WTCHF USD 22.09 (last trade 2026-09-23, thin) / 0.7026 = A$31.44 vs ASX A$31.33, a 0.35% tie -- confirms rate, direction and quote basis. The rate is not moved by refresh_price.py; re-date it on the next update.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD-built, because the flows are USD. Cost of equity: US 10y ~4.3% + relevered beta ~1.2 x 5.5% ERP = ~10.9% (house USD tech default 10.5%, +0.4pp for post-e2open leverage via beta, not an ad-hoc premium). Cost of debt: FY26 finance costs 139.6 on ~2.2bn drawn SFA term loans (SOFR + margin, 1,275m swapped) = ~6.3% pre-tax, ~4.8% after tax. Weights at market: equity ~US$7.45bn (A$31.33 x 338.4m x 0.7026), debt 2.22bn -> 77/23. WACC = 0.77 x 10.9 + 0.23 x 4.8 = 9.5%. One WACC for all scenarios; governance, ACCC and e2open-attrition risk is charged in the bear flows and a 30% bear weight, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease payments (FY26 principal 13.2 + ~2 interest = ~1.0% of revenue) charged via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (13.8 + 38.2 = 52.0) EXCLUDED from net debt; da_pct excludes right-of-use depreciation.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating SaaS company; dcf-methods routing row 1, plus owner-fcf-adaptations for the USD-reporting / AUD-quote split and leases). First valuation of this ticker -- no prior DCF or memory entry. FY0 BASE: FY26 revenue 1,395.9 contains only 11 months of e2open (541.2; completed 3-Aug-2025), so the 12th month (~49) sits inside FY27 guided growth of 6-10% -- implied organic growth is only ~2.5-6.5%. FY26 underlying EBITDA 644.5 (46.2%) is after 62.3 expensed SBC; the component build uses pre-SBC EBITDA (706.8 = 50.6%) and charges full SBC 80.3 separately. FY27 guidance midpoint 752.5 / 1,510 = 49.8% post-expensed-SBC ~ 54% pre-SBC, which is the base year-1 margin. D&A path EXCLUDES acquired-intangible amortisation (~108 pre-tax; 81.1 after tax) and ROU depreciation: e2open was a share acquisition with no tax step-up, so acquired amortisation gives no cash-tax shield; ~6% of revenue is capitalised-development amortisation plus PP&E depreciation. OWNER FCF FY26 = reported FCF 356.3 (OCF 509.6 - capex 153.3; interest paid 120.1 is in financing so this is pre-interest) - SBC 80.3 - interest income 0 (net DEBT of 1,876.5, so finance income 6.0 is not stripped; it is small and offsets nothing in the bridge). FY26 OCF carries 43.1 restructuring and 35.8 M&A cash (one-off) and a ~70 working-capital outflow tied to e2open integration; the forward build does not repeat them. Cash tax is modelled UNLEVERED (22% -> 24% on EBIT): FY26's 54.4 paid was depressed by ~35 of interest deductions and ~17 of restructuring deductions, which belong to the financing and one-off lines, not the operating flow. e2open's US tax attributes (NOLs subject to s382) are an unmodelled upside. BUYBACKS: none; the flat count is a modelling convention funded by new issuance to the employee trust (~0.4%/yr), so a non-repurchaser in DUOL terms. Net debt at face value of drawn SFA loans (2,220.0 per note 15; carrying 2,187.4 is net of capitalised fees). Post-balance-date FRDM.ai (24.3 incl. contingent) treated as value-neutral asset-for-cash; FY26 final dividend (8.8c) not deducted (paid to holders of record 14-Sep, price is ex-dividend).
inputs.history_fx_basis: USD history for CAGRs: FY21-FY25 from the company's own USD five-year summary (FY25 Annual Report p.102; implied translation rates FY21 0.7429, FY22 0.7291, FY23 0.6761, FY24 0.6563 AUD->USD); FY26 as reported USD. Flows (FCF, EPS) translated at those average rates; balance-sheet equity at 30-June spot (Jun-21 0.7505, Jun-23 0.6630, RBA). The Metrics.csv keeps FY2016-H1 FY2024 in AUD by design (redenomination, not an error); no AUD and USD figure is mixed in one series here.

equity_bridge.item: Contingent and deferred acquisition consideration (fair value)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 Annual Report fair-value hierarchy table: contingent 46.4 (level 3) + deferred 0.3, USD m

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 guidance midpoint (6-10%) and the base-case first-five-year revenue path; every historical CAGR is inflated by the debt-funded e2open acquisition (FY26 revenue +79%) and none describes forward organic growth
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 18.5% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 29.9% (and equity 3yr 15.6% vs revenue 3yr 36.2%). Cause: e2open was 100% debt-funded, so revenue jumped with no matching equity; EPS 3yr CAGR is only 6.8% because the acquisition's interest and acquired amortisation offset its revenue. Equity CAGR not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR (30.8% 3yr) is in line with reported FCF (30.2%), so SBC is not growing faster than cash flow on a 3-year view; on 5 years owner FCF (30.7%) slightly lags reported (31.8%) -- SBC rose from 22.1 AUD (FY21, 4.4% of revenue) to 80.3 USD (5.75%). Interest income stripped from owner FCF in net-cash years (FY16-FY25), not in FY26 (net debt).

base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-SBC underlying EBITDA. FY26 50.6%; FY27 guidance 49-51% post-expensed-SBC ~ 54% pre-SBC. Mature 59.5% = CargoWise ~62% pre-SBC (FY25 standalone 57.2% pre-SBC, rising on AI Transformation savings of 34m + 17m run-rate) blended with e2open ~50% (36.5% FY26 post synergies of 64m, targeting WiseTech's product-led model). Part of guided margin expansion is higher development capitalisation, which is why capex rises in years 1-3.

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 lands at the guidance midpoint (8% revenue, ~50% underlying EBITDA). CargoWise keeps compounding ~10-11% as the 61 secured LGFF rollouts (over 75% of contracted volume not yet live) go live and CVP pricing beds in, while e2open stabilises roughly flat as attrition fades into the product-led model. Group growth holds ~8% for five years then glides to 4%; pre-SBC margin rises to ~59.5% on the 64m e2open synergies and 51m AI Transformation run-rate savings. Leverage (~2.9x EBITDA) is paid down from FCF; the ACCC investigation ends without changing the commercial model.
scenario_narratives.bull: Upper-end guidance and beyond: CVP lifts monetisation of the base, agentic AI inside CargoWise (six agents live, targeting ~50% labour savings for forwarders) is priced as a product rather than given away, VerifyWise, TradeWise and customs/government add a new leg, and e2open returns to growth as a cross-sell channel into 500,000 connected enterprises. Revenue compounds 10-12% for five years and the group reaches CargoWise-like ~63% pre-SBC margins.
scenario_narratives.bear: The market's read of the guidance is right: organic growth is really ~3-5% once the e2open 12th month is removed, e2open subscription attrition persists, and the CVP transition (2H26 'refinements') and competitor probing of CargoWise lock-in slow LGFF monetisation. The ACCC investigation forces changes to pricing/contract terms, and governance/founder-continuity friction slows execution. Growth runs 4-4.5%, margins stall at ~54% pre-SBC with SBC sticky at ~5.5-6%, and the exit multiple is capped at 15x as a slower, leveraged software roll-up.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% default: an open ACCC investigation (search warrant 19-Aug-2026) with an unknown remedy, e2open still losing subscription revenue, first-ever leverage (~US$2.2bn drawn) and unresolved founder/governance risk are four independent downside axes. Base 50% because FY27 guidance was issued after the synergies were already banked. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things at once (CVP uplift, AI monetisation, e2open turning to growth, new-product adoption).

valuation_philosophy.summary: WiseTech is valued as a USD-reporting, AUD-quoted owner-FCF compounder that has just levered up for a large, lower-quality acquisition. SBC (~5.75% of revenue) is expensed in the flows and the diluted count held flat. The FY26 base has one-offs on both sides (11 months of e2open, restructuring and M&A cash out, an interest-depressed tax bill), so the forward flows are built from components anchored to FY27 guidance rather than from FY26 FCF. Risk is charged once: one USD WACC of 9.5%, with governance, ACCC and e2open risk carried in the bear flows and its 30% weight.
key_risks_to_valuation: ACCC investigation outcome (penalty and/or forced change to CargoWise commercial terms) -- unquantified, not in the equity bridge
e2open subscription attrition continues and its margin never converges toward WiseTech's
Organic growth: FY27 guidance of 6-10% includes ~3.5pp from the 12th month of e2open
Leverage: US$2.22bn term loans maturing 2027-2030; Tranche A (572.5m) due Jul-2027 needs refinancing
AUDUSD: IV is USD-based; a 5% AUD appreciation cuts the AUD value per share ~5%
Terminal value share of EV is high (long-duration software); see required-return table
